# Set-ZbxHostPrototype

## SYNOPSIS

Changes a host prototype.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxHostPrototype [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHostPrototype>[]> [[-Name] <string>] [-GroupPrototype <ZabbixHostPrototypeUpdateGroupPrototypeRequest[]>] [-Uuid <string>] [-DisplayName <string>] [-CustomInterfaces <ZabbixHostPrototypeInterfaceMode>] [-Status <ZabbixHostStatus>] [-Discover <ZabbixDiscoverMode>] [-Interface <ZabbixHostPrototypeInterfaceRequest[]>] [-GroupLink <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHostGroup>[]>] [-Template <ZabbixReference<ZabbixTemplate>[]>] [-Tag <ZabbixTagRequest[]>] [-Macro <ZabbixHostPrototypeUpdateMacroRequest[]>] [-InventoryMode <ZabbixHostInventoryMode>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-PipedRecord <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A host prototype is the pattern a discovery rule turns into one host per entity it finds, such as a virtual machine of a hypervisor. The Set-ZbxHostPrototype cmdlet changes the host prototypes given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with hostprototype.update; a field whose parameter is not given keeps its value. Every host prototype the pipeline brings is changed in one call when the pipeline ends, and -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name. The command writes nothing unless -PassThru is given, which reads the changed host prototypes back and writes them; -WhatIf shows what would change.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Change a host prototype

```powershell
Set-ZbxHostPrototype -InputObject '{#VM.NAME}' -Status Disabled
```

Makes the host prototype {#VM.NAME} create its hosts disabled.

### Example 2: Change a host prototype and write the result

```powershell
Set-ZbxHostPrototype -InputObject '{#VM.NAME}' -Status Disabled -PassThru
```

The same change with -PassThru, which reads the host prototype {#VM.NAME} back from the server and writes it; without it the command writes nothing.
